adapter_id_cases.json -- vendored oracle, provenance
====================================================

Source:        chiplet-spec, conformance/fixtures/adapter_id_cases.json
Pinned commit: 41264bc (chiplet-spec; local at vendor time. chiplet-spec never
               rebases or force-pushes, so this object is final; the remote sha
               is the same one once its dev is pushed. Flip this line to
               "on origin/dev" once that push is confirmed.)
Content sha256: 0364a6f2a2da84f9651af8283b1c456638e6897d174d105f271ed46ddfb80eb1
Vendored:      byte-identical, no edits.

Do NOT edit this file here. Add or change cases UPSTREAM in chiplet-spec (where
the spec's own conformance test proves the set against chiplet.schema.json), then
re-vendor. per-repo-cicd owns the re-vendor and the lockstep pin.

Why it exists: the *.adapter fields of chiplet.schema.json (interposer.adapter,
interconnect.adapter) are the id pattern PLUS a ".drc" negative. This one shared
accept/reject set is what every implementation of that contract parity-tests
against -- adk_registry.validate_adapter_id (here), the kicad plugin's producer
check, chiplet-studio, and the Mosaic engine -- so no consumer verdict can
silently diverge from run_drc's. One semantics, three roads, one oracle.
